scope_note: Deliberately varied 20-entity source-yield sample. This is a source-strategy measurement, not population-statistical inference and not authorization for bulk ingestion. Approximate model counts describe discoverable production-sailboat identities on the cited source surfaces, not canonical HullQ admissions.

method.selection: Verified manufacturer/yard records chosen to span active and historical entities, high-volume and specialist builders, monohulls and multihulls, multiple macro-regions, strong official archives, contract-yard cases, and difficult archival-only cases.
method.rights_rule: Public readability is discovery evidence only. Unless a separate licence or terms review clears systematic reuse, later systematic use remains REQUIRES_REVIEW.
method.overlap_probe: probe_model_names are compared later only by exact preferred-label equality against AUTO_ADMIT candidates in the accepted SLICE-0017 and SLICE-0018 manifests. Alias/case-only signals are reported as unresolved possible overlap, never forced matches.

entities.sample_reason: Large active builder with a strong official history plus a broad manufacturer-hosted brochure archive.
entities.model_list_mode: explicit archive index plus current-range pages
entities.expansion_pattern: index plus linked model brochures/pages
entities.measurement_note: Official brochure archive exposes dozens of historical models; current model pages and brochures usually provide LOA/LWL/beam/draft/displacement. Keel, rig, material and variant detail generally requires following the model-specific page or brochure.

entities.sample_reason: Historical builder whose surviving owner archive preserves a near-model-index and original factory documentation.
entities.model_list_mode: explicit owner-archive model table
entities.expansion_pattern: model index plus linked original brochures and model pages
entities.measurement_note: The owners' archive exposes dedicated pages and original brochures for many models. Basic dimensions, displacement, ballast and rig data are commonly available; variants and some appendage details still require per-model review.

entities.sample_reason: Contract-manufacturing yard that built for multiple brands; deliberately tests yard-to-brand reconstruction rather than a clean consumer-brand archive.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: 20+ reconstructable across brand histories; no safe single-yard total
entities.model_list_mode: reconstructed across J/Boats, Freedom, Alerion and other brand histories
entities.expansion_pattern: multi-source relationship expansion
entities.measurement_note: TPI is valuable as a physical-builder identity but poor as a single model-discovery endpoint. Brand histories clearly establish J/Boats, Freedom and Alerion production relationships; model-level technical facts should be sourced from the corresponding brand/model archives, not inferred from TPI alone.

entities.sample_reason: Exceptionally strong official heritage model index with detailed model pages.
entities.model_list_mode: explicit official heritage index
entities.expansion_pattern: one index plus linked model pages
entities.measurement_note: Official heritage pages commonly retain years built, hull counts and LOA/LWL/beam/draft/displacement. The archive is one of the cleanest observed manufacturer surfaces for identity expansion and later technical enrichment.

entities.sample_reason: Defunct high-volume builder with an unusually rich owners-association wiki and brochure archive.
entities.model_list_mode: explicit owner-wiki lists and brochure index
entities.expansion_pattern: archive index plus linked brochures/specifications
entities.measurement_note: The archive exposes many model brochures, specifications and keel/rig variants. Variant naming and corporate-era changes require review even though raw source depth is high.

entities.sample_reason: Tests production-yard discovery where useful model identities live under Southerly and Vancouver rather than the yard name.
entities.model_list_mode: reconstructed across brand histories
entities.critical_technical_fields_availability: strong for variable-draft/keel concepts; mixed otherwise
entities.expansion_pattern: multi-source brand/yard expansion
entities.measurement_note: Southerly history gives a sequence from the 28 through later 32/38/42RST/420/47/49/535/57RS and other models; Vancouver history adds another model family. The main cost is identity/production relationship resolution, not lack of model evidence.

entities.sample_reason: Large active builder with generation/range-based official heritage pages that can yield many identities cheaply.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: 60+ from sampled official heritage generations; broader total higher
entities.model_list_mode: explicit official range/generation indexes
entities.expansion_pattern: range indexes plus linked model pages/documents
entities.measurement_note: Oceanis and First heritage pages expose dense identity lists and many basic dimensions. Technical configuration details and reused model numbers across generations require later model-level resolution.

entities.sample_reason: Active catamaran builder with strong current specifications and useful but less index-like historical material.
entities.model_list_mode: mixed current index plus historical timeline reconstruction
entities.core_dimensions_availability: strong for current models; partial historical
entities.expansion_pattern: current index plus history and linked model pages
entities.measurement_note: Current sailing-catamaran pages carry strong dimension and displacement data. Historical identity yield is good but is reconstructed from company history rather than one exhaustive previous-model index.

entities.sample_reason: Specialist builder whose official timeline and current technical pages expose both historical identities and configuration-rich new boats.
entities.model_list_mode: official timeline plus current model pages
entities.expansion_pattern: timeline plus linked model pages
entities.measurement_note: The current site exposes dimensions and configuration detail, including swing-keel draft ranges on the Wauquiez 55. Historical coverage is useful but less uniform than the current pages.

entities.sample_reason: Difficult defunct-yard case where a specialist historical source is more useful than an official archive.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: 8 production identities plus one prototype in the measured list
entities.model_list_mode: explicit specialist-secondary historical list
entities.expansion_pattern: historical list followed by per-model secondary/class expansion
entities.measurement_note: The historical source provides a compact model chronology, but dimensions and appendage/rig/material details require separate sources. This is useful for identity discovery but poor for automated technical enrichment.

entities.sample_reason: Active builder with official previous-model pages, long company history and strong current technical data.
entities.model_list_mode: explicit previous-model page plus history/current range
entities.expansion_pattern: previous-model index plus linked model pages
entities.measurement_note: Official previous-model and history surfaces expose a broad identity set. Current model pages include detailed rig and sail information, making Elan useful for both identity and controlled technical enrichment pilots.

entities.sample_reason: Negative-control style yard: very strong evidence of large-scale sailboat manufacture, but model identities are marketed under Jeanneau/Beneteau rather than indexed by the yard.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: not safely countable from yard surface; official site states >30 motor+sail models combined
entities.model_list_mode: not enumerated by yard; requires brand-production crosswalk
entities.expansion_pattern: yard evidence then external brand/model crosswalk
entities.automation_suitability: low for model discovery; high for confirming yard role
entities.measurement_note: The official site states more than 30 motor and sailing models and roughly 4,000 units/year under Jeanneau and Beneteau trademarks, but it does not enumerate the sail-only subset. This source should confirm production relationships, not mint model identities by inference.

entities.sample_reason: Long-running Italian Grand Soleil yard with official heritage timeline and technically rich current model pages.
entities.model_list_mode: official heritage timeline plus current range
entities.expansion_pattern: heritage timeline plus linked current model pages
entities.measurement_note: The heritage timeline yields many Grand Soleil identities; current pages expose dimensions, displacement and draft variants. Reused numeric model names across generations create a BoatDesign/generation-resolution burden.

entities.sample_reason: Historical Italian yard preserved by a dedicated recognized historical club with model pages and specifications.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: 11+ in the >9 m category alone; additional smaller models exist
entities.model_list_mode: explicit historical-club category indexes
entities.expansion_pattern: category index plus linked model pages
entities.measurement_note: Sampled historical-club pages expose build year, length, beam, sail area, displacement and ballast. Keel/rudder/material detail is less uniform and still needs page-level review.

entities.sample_reason: Strong official previous-model ecosystem with current specs, manufacturer PDFs and even parts evidence useful for appendage configuration.
entities.model_list_mode: official previous-model pages; recognized dealer index helps navigation
entities.critical_technical_fields_availability: strong relative to sample, with parts/brochure expansion
entities.expansion_pattern: previous-model pages plus PDFs and parts archive
entities.measurement_note: Previous-model pages and manufacturer-hosted PDFs offer strong dimensions and production chronology. The official parts ecosystem can provide unusually specific evidence such as rudder/skeg components, but those facts should remain source-linked rather than inferred across models.

entities.sample_reason: Premium active yard with authoritative heritage timeline, current model index and manufacturer brochures.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: 25+ readily discoverable from current and heritage surfaces; broader historical catalogue is larger
entities.model_list_mode: mixed current index plus heritage timeline
entities.core_dimensions_availability: strong current; partial-to-strong via historical brochures
entities.expansion_pattern: current index/timeline plus linked brochures
entities.measurement_note: The official current index is structured and the heritage timeline identifies many important historical models, but the entire older corpus is not exposed as one exhaustive machine-friendly list. Brochure expansion is needed for deeper technical facts.

entities.sample_reason: Difficult archival case with unusually valuable direct family/yard history preserved as a PDF and class/owners material.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: 4 explicit series identities in the direct history (BB11, BB17, BB35, Yngling)
entities.model_list_mode: explicit direct-history narrative
entities.expansion_pattern: direct PDF plus class/owners sources per model
entities.measurement_note: The direct family history establishes roughly 1,200 BB11, 350 BB17, three BB35 and later about 2,000 Ynglings, while also resolving the yard's 1984 closure. Technical dimensions and appendage details require separate class/model sources.

entities.sample_reason: Australian-origin active catamaran manufacturer with a long official model history and current technical specification documents from multinational production facilities.
entities.model_list_mode: official history/timeline plus current range
entities.expansion_pattern: history plus current model pages/PDFs
entities.measurement_note: The official 40-year history enumerates many generations; current specification PDFs include construction/material, steering/rudder and rig details. Historical production moved across Australia, Vietnam and Türkiye, so production-location relationships must remain time-aware.

entities.sample_reason: Large South African physical yard with a strong official pedigree count but consumer-facing model identities spread across Leopard/Moorings/Sunsail brands.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: 24 sailing-catamaran model identities stated by the yard
entities.model_list_mode: official pedigree count plus brand/model reconstruction
entities.core_dimensions_availability: strong on current manufacturer model pages
entities.expansion_pattern: yard pedigree plus linked/related brand model pages
entities.measurement_note: The official achievements surface states a pedigree of 24 sailing-catamaran models and more than 3,132 catamarans launched through April 2026. Current Leopard pages provide rich LOA/LWL/beam/draft/displacement/sail and layout data, but brand-to-yard identity relationships must be explicit.

entities.sample_reason: Historical New Zealand builder with good designer/founder and owner evidence but no surviving official yard archive.
entities.discoverable_model_identity_estimate: at least 11 simultaneous production designs at peak; broader historical range exceeds that
entities.model_list_mode: reconstructed from founder/designer and owner/historical sources
entities.expansion_pattern: multi-source historical reconstruction
entities.measurement_note: Founder Peter Smith's biography and recognized historical/owner material establish a substantial production range, with around 170 Cavalier 32s and 84 Cavalier 39s reported. Licensed builds and successor Export Yachts activity make exact physical-builder attribution a later identity-resolution task.
